en: Neural networks and deep learning is a
specialized form of machine learning
where data is used to build an artificial
virtual neural network, essentially trying
to reproduce how the human brain works,
which you can also think of as complex
networks of neurons talking to each other.
And we try to replicate this
on computers virtually
and kind of rebuild how a human thinks
virtually, therefore.
Now, a neural network is a so-called
parameterized model composed of connected
computational layers.
And that simply means that you funnel data,
let's say the text you're sending to
ChatGPT, through multiple layers of
parameters, which are in the end just
numbers, you could say, to generate a new
outcome. In case of ChatGPT, you would be
generating new text. If you're thinking
about a product recommendation algorithm,
you would feed in, for example, a list of
products a user bought in the past. And then
through all these layers, all these
connections and weights and parameters in
that model,
it would spit out a new list of recommended
products. And how are these numbers derived?
Then, well, that happens during the training
where
data, example training data, is used to
predict outputs which are also maybe known
in advance during training and to build a
model. So to build that network such that we
can predict the right values based on the
input data. During training, you know both
the output and the input data potentially.
So therefore you can of course tweak the
model until the output is in line with what
you expect. And then you can take that
trained neural network and put it in
production and use it on unknown user data
on the products you actually bought, for
example, and then spit out those
recommendations. So the idea really just is
that we rebuild how the human brain works.
And large language models, for example, do
use this neural network approach.
